population.definition: Juba County (not the city alone), census of 22 April 2008, as relayed by citypopulation.de from the South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics. No census since 2008; 2017 projection for the county is 525,953 and does not account for migration or displacement.

source.title: Juba (Central Equatoria, South Sudan) - population statistics
source.publisher: citypopulation.de (citing South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics)
source.quote: 2008 census (April 22, 2008): 368,436 residents; 2017 projection: 525,953

facts.claim: Juba grew from a mission station near a small Bari village on the White Nile; the site was chosen in 1927 as a new administrative headquarters (Mongalla Province) by Arthur Wallace Skrine.

source.title: To the Juba Wharf (Juba in the Making)
source.author: Brendan Tuttle
source.quote: The site was chosen as a new administrative headquarters in 1927 by Arthur Wallace Skrine

facts.claim: Juba is the capital of Central Equatoria State and was the seat of the Government of Southern Sudan.

source.title: City limits: urbanisation and vulnerability in Sudan - Juba case study
source.publisher: Humanitarian Policy Group, Overseas Development Institute (ODI)
source.author: Ellen Martin and Irina Mosel
source.quote: Juba is the seat of the Government of Southern Sudan (GoSS) as well as the capital of Central Equatoria State (CES).

facts.claim: Juba was chosen as capital of Southern Sudan partly as a gesture of inclusiveness, since it lies in Bari heartland; it already had an airport, water and was closer to neighbouring countries. Ram Chiel had been the favoured option.

source.title: City limits: urbanisation and vulnerability in Sudan - Juba case study
source.publisher: Humanitarian Policy Group, Overseas Development Institute (ODI)
source.author: Ellen Martin and Irina Mosel
source.quote: Juba is located in the heartland of the Bari people, so selecting it as the new capital was seen as a gesture of inclusiveness

facts.claim: South Sudan declared independence on 9 July 2011, with celebrations in Juba.

source.title: South Sudan becomes world's newest nation
source.author: News Agencies
source.quote: A mood of joy and celebration swept through its capital Juba at midnight on Friday

facts.claim: Plans exist to move the capital to Ramciel; in 2017 South Sudan signed an agreement with Morocco for construction there, with no clear start date.

source.title: Morocco funds Ramciel construction
source.author: Obaj Shago
source.quote: South Sudan has signed an agreement with Morocco for the construction of the new capital in Ramciel.

places.name: Dr John Garang Mausoleum
places.what: The mausoleum and memorial park in Juba honours John Garang, the liberation leader, and has hosted national ceremonies. Independence celebrations on 9 July 2011 were held there and a statue was unveiled.

places.name: Konyo Konyo Market
places.what: Konyo-Konyo is one of Juba's major markets and a distribution point for goods across South Sudan. It has faced congestion, fires and redevelopment proposals.

source.title: Developer proposes to modernize Juba's Konyo-Konyo Market
source.quote: Konyo-Konyo is one of Juba's major markets and an important distribution point for goods across South Sudan.

facts.label: Problems

source.title: Developer proposes to modernize Juba's Konyo-Konyo Market

places.name: Freedom Bridge and the White Nile crossing
places.what: The Freedom Bridge is a steel arch bridge over the Nile in Juba, opened in 2022. It supplements the older Juba Bridge, a prefabricated crossing.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: 560 m long, first arched steel bridge in the country to span the Nile

source.title: Completion of the Freedom Bridge: South Sudan's Long-awaited Symbol of Peace and Freedom
source.quote: the first arched steel bridge in the country to span the Nile River

places.name: Jebel Kujur
places.what: Jebel Kujur is a hill and wooded grassland area immediately south-west of Juba, recognised as a Key Biodiversity Area. It lies under severe pressure from the nearby town.

source.title: Juba (6818)
source.quote: lies immediately south-west of the town of Juba in southern Sudan

source.title: Juba (6818)
source.quote: The vegetation is wooded grassland in which common tree species include Balanites aegyptiaca

source.title: Juba (6818)
source.quote: Threats to the site are severe, due to its proximity to Juba town.
